rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> two-year split-plot field experiment at Ludhiana (2018, 2019) with three irrigation methods (SSD, SD, flood) and four weed control treatments. Q2: Results, Tables 1<U+2013>4 <U+2013> in 2018 total weed density under SSD at 30 DAS was lower than SD and flood; at 60 DAS flood had higher total weed density than SD and SSD; total weed biomass at 60 DAS was lower under SD and SSD than flood (21, 36, 45 g/m2), with SSD lowest; Abstract states SSD had lower weed density and biomass in the drier year. Q7: Discussion <U+2013> authors state that in 2019 no differential irrigation was applied because rain was sufficient and well distributed, hence irrigation methods showed no effect on weed density or biomass; the weed-reducing effect of drip appeared only in the drier 2018 season when differential irrigations were given (conclusion: in 2019 all irrigation methods at par).
rows.notes: The study supports only the weed-growth part of the claim; it reports nothing on pests or fungus incidence. Its stated mechanism is a dry upper soil surface under subsurface drip, not a dry plant canopy as the passage says. Soil water was measured by TDR only for the water balance; no surface-moisture data under each irrigation method are reported, so the mechanism is asserted rather than measured (Q4 no). Single site, single crop, plot scale; weed assessment by one method (quadrat counts and dry biomass). No SD/SE/CI reported, only Tukey letter groupings. Q7 is a judgement call: the dry-season/differential-irrigation condition is stated as the explanation for presence vs absence of the effect rather than as an explicit requirement. No limitations section.
